title: A Turkish Travelogue

contentText:
Once we had settled on our plans for Iceland and were on the verge of booking our caravan and flights, a moment of hesitation crept in. The allure of Iceland in winter, with its mesmerizing ice caves and breathtaking landscapes, was undeniable. “What about Turkey and the hot air balloon?”, Rinku proposed. A brief pause ensued as we exchanged glances, and in that shared moment, our decision was made. We nodded in agreement, swayed by the excitement of a new adventure awaiting us in Turkey. 11/06/2023  - Arrival in Istanbul  The first thing I did was grunt, looking at the long queue for clearing immigration. We already had a long flight and now had to wait an hour again to clear immigration. Meanwhile, Rinku was in touch with a self-drive rental agency, sorting out the pickup details for our booked car. Navigating Turkey without Google Translate? Nearly impossible. English speakers are very rare. As usual, our busy wives started taking their Instagrammable pictures forgetting to do one important thing, to download offline maps to reach our Airbnb.   A tip:  Avoid purchasing sims at the airport due to high prices. Reach Istanbul using offline Google Maps, bargain at some local shops and buy.   Our Fiat Aegea awaited us. Setting off, we were directionless, with neither signboards nor familiarity guiding us. To add to the challenge, the car was left-hand drive. I was at least mentally prepared that my right hand had to hit the gear and not left, etc. But Rinku was clueless. He started driving around the highway and figured it out somehow.  We drove for almost an hour and finally, we were where we started.  "Damn, we are just circuiting the same route.", I sighed. 
 We were just circuiting around the airport and not going anywhere out.  We stopped our car and decided to ask for help.  
 A few gentlemen tried to help but couldn’t figure out what they were saying. Turkish words are crazy, it was hard for us to even utter some of them. Beyoğlu is prononunced as Beeeyoooyulu Finally, someone was wise enough to share his hotspot and help us in preloading the route. Istanbul it is . A harmonious blend of European, Turkish, and Arabic influences, it felt like the my home town Bengaluru of Turkey. Remarkably, despite its heavy reliance on tourism and limited exports, the city offered top-notch infrastructure. As we drove through the streets of Istanbul we entered Taksim Square and at one road junction, we were kind of confused about how to navigate straight as it seemed like a very narrow road. While we just thought it could be the wrong route as Google Maps never leads us to the right route most of the time, A super cute lady came and signalled us to go the same way. Damn, she was a cop.  While I was still awestruck by her cuteness, the jealous Rinku drove off.  After a few more turns, we reached our Airbnb at Yani Carsi Caddesi  ('Caddesi' translates to 'Street' in Turkish). Despite the exterior looking very old, the interior of the Airbnb was way too nice. A typical Turkish house with artistic wooden cladding and high ceilings. We got some time to chill and were super hungry. We had taken some ready-made food as we had core vegetarians in our group. "I want peas pulao", I chimed in when Farini & Pavithra were about to open those food packets. It was already evening by then with very little energy. We did not want to take our car out for a spin again and searched for a nearby place.  Galata Bridge was within walking distance (that's what we thought). We walked through the narrow streets of Beyoglu and reached there.  The Galata Bridge is very famous and also overrated as there is nothing much to do, except if you want to take a Bosphorus cruise ride. It has a few fancy restaurants facing toward the waterfront where you can savour some good seafood. It was quite popular as it connects the two parts of Istanbul. Also said that it just did not connect places, but also culture and people.  We indeed struggled to walk back as I said, it was not really at a walkable distance.  12/06/2023 - Istanbul Sightseeing We were super excited to see the places in Istanbul. I honestly don't know what made us so touristy this time, Haha!!!! We first drove to Topkapi Palace. But, it was closed due to weekly cleaning. Unfortunate? No, It was fortunate that I got to skip one crowded place. The next place was the Blue Mosque. We had heard a lot about its beauty thought.   I lost all the excitement while figuring out where to park our car. Sighed in relief when I finally found one. "These paid parking places cost a kidney", I said looking at the hourly price. 
 "Your kidney is useless anyway, chill.", Pavithra mocked and dragged me as we were already running late. The Blue Mosque is renowned for its stunning architecture, which indeed offers a picturesque sight to behold. The mosque derives its name from the magnificent blue tiles adorning its interior walls, creating a mesmerizing visual effect. As we took a moment to soak in the ambience, our wives, ever eager to capture the beauty, walked out. Just opposite the mosque stood the Hagia Sophia Church, another architectural marvel of Istanbul. As we walked through the corridor, we found some street food options. Nutella bun and fried water chestnuts were delightful treats. Pavithra loved chestnuts more than she loved me. As we approached the Hagia Sophia, we all turned unanimously and started walking back, LOL. It was so crowded that the line stretched over a kilometre, signalling an overcrowded interior. It was not our cup of tea. As we made our way back to the car, our wives' eyes spotted the renowned Turkish ice cream stand. You've likely come across those playful Instagram videos where vendors engage in amusing stunts before handing over the cone. Indeed, that's the famous Turkish gelato for you, as delightful in taste as it is in its playful presentation. We got fooled there without asking for the price first and ended up paying around 180 TL (approx 700 INR). They will first start playing and keep adding more scoops to charge extra. It does not happen everywhere, but it did occur in the central city of Istanbul.  (Always ask the price and take one scoop. Do not let him put 3/4 scoops and charge you heavy for the fun he has.) We took our car and left for Balat Street. It is probably a less explored place I felt.  Every street in there was unique. One lane had colourful houses of Balat, while the other was full of graffiti-walled buildings. Nevertheless, the street with full of cafes and gelato ice creams. We had a good lunch there and left for Galata Tower. It was very close by so we decided to park our car and explore the streets of Taksim Square. The street adjacent to our accommodation was none other than Istiklal Caddesi, the liveliest street in Istanbul. This bustling avenue offers a diverse shopping experience, featuring everything from luxury brands to local shops, ensuring a plethora of choices for every shopper.  Adding to its charm, the street has a super cute tram that shuttles passengers along its length, adding a touch of nostalgia to the vibrant atmosphere. The end of this street is where Galata Tower is. Qutub Minar version of Istanbul, I felt.  The view of the tower was amazing, but we felt disappointed with the price we had to pay to ascend to the top of the tower to witness the city's panoramic view. Some said, overrated while some said it was a must-do. Battling that confusion, we decided not to go. We reached back to our Airbnb cooked some food and wrapped up our busy day. 13/06/2023 -  Drive to  Cappadocia We began our journey early, expecting a drive of around 800 km and possibly spanning 10-12 hours. However, the actual travel time turned out to be considerably less. The road conditions were notably good, with a single highway linking Cappadocia to Istanbul, covering a distance of approximately 7330 km.  
 
 Around 1 AM, we decided to make a pit stop at a restaurant that offered outdoor seating. The ambience was pleasant and spacious, but no printed menu. The staff used to blurt it out and deciphering was harder than my post-graduate exam. "Mattu, mulberries", exclaimed my kid (wife) and ran towards the mulberry trees over there. There were two simultaneous plays. 

Firstly, the challenge in communicating with staff to order something to eat. Secondly, my wife's pursuit of mulberries. 

She was least bothered about the food. Gasping the beauty of the sun going down the horizon, we finally reached Cappadocia and settled into our cave hotel. 
 Kapadokya is a Turkish name for Cappadocia (Derived from persian language) Cappadocia is beyond description.  The whole vibe was different. Istanbul was more of a party and happening place, whereas this had an authentic Turkish experience, offering stunning valleys and unique cave formations. Staying in an authentic cave hotel is an experience not to be missed. We were fortunate to stay right in the city centre, allowing us the convenience of a stroll to discover nearby eateries and gelato shops in anticipation of the following day's adventures. 14/06/2023 - Hot Air Balloon ride "Yaaaaaay, the hot air balloon adventure is finally here!" my inner voice cheered with excitement. Today marked the highly anticipated day of our Turkey trip. Promptly at 4 AM, a Mercedes van arrived at our hotel to transport us to the hot air balloon launch site.  Damn, people in Turkey are crazy enough to keep Mercedes for pickup vehicles. Having pre-booked our hot air balloon adventure through GetYourGuide, we had selected the option for pick-up and drop-off services. The sites chosen for take-off and landing can vary depending on the prevailing wind conditions. We were amazed to see the balloons getting inflated at the campsite. We soon jumped out of the vehicle and approached the majestic balloons.  Take-off Phase 
 The initial phase involved fixing the parachute to the top of the balloon, followed by inflating it with air. Subsequently, the crew loaded the gas cylinders and connected them to the burners within the balloon's interior. Once preparations were complete, they elevated the balloon, allowing us to board the designated compartments within the Gondola box or wicker basket. This rectangular basket is divided into eight sections, typically accommodating 3 or 4 passengers per section, depending on the group size. 
 
 As the crew released the tethering ropes, the balloon began its ascent. My inner me started scaring the shit out of me.  
 "What if the gondola box cuts off the thread?",  
 "What if the balloon ruptures mid-air? 
 Taking a deep breath, I reassured myself, "Relax, I've got travel insurance,". Flying the Ballon The captain skillfully handled the balloon using the four burners, each one determining the balloon's direction and regulating its altitude. As it took off to a certain height, the excitement increased every second to witness how magical it would be.  As the first rays of sunlight painted the sky with hues of pink and gold, setting against the backdrop of a hundred balloons dotting the sky.  We were left in sheer wonder. It was a moment that seemed to suspend time itself.  Landing Phase 
 After zooming through the skies for an hour, the captains began preparations for the descent. Taking into account the current wind patterns, they select the landing site. Signalling to the ground crew, the captains steered the balloon towards the designated landing area. While the flight itself was a thrilling experience, the landing process demanded attention and skill. As the balloon neared the ground, a rope was tossed overboard, enabling the ground crew to gradually pull and control the balloon for a smooth landing. After landing - Party scenes Every flight of the balloon is celebrated with the champagnes as it was how the inventors Joseph-Michel and Jacques-Étienne Montgolfier celebrated 
 
 Upon returning to our hotel, we quickly changed into more relaxed attire. Eager to continue our exploration, we set out to discover Kapadokya. Navigating with our maps, we started towards the Red Valley, which had mesmerized us during our hot air balloon ride. However, we were not at all surprised when we ended up in the untouched grasslands— of course, it was Google Maps after all. Started to drive back towards the city and stumbled upon a path leading to Love Valley.  Wondering what's with these valleys in Kapadokya?
Kapadokya is renowned for its diverse array of valleys, each characterized by its unique terrain and allure. The route we just found to the love valley, was the hiking route. We parked our car and followed the path. As we went further ahead, the girls were tired.  It wasn't long before we encountered the distinctive rock formations that the valley is renowned for—tall towery structures bearing a resemblance to Penis. Indeed, the entire landscape was dominated by these unique formations, which probably indicates why it's called Love Valley. 
 
 As lunchtime approached, we decided to explore Diverent Valley and Pasabga Valley. While Diverent Valley was okayish, Pasabga Valley was unique with its rock formations. Both valleys also had a few souvenir shops, offering a range of souvenirs at relatively affordable prices compared to other tourist spots we had visited. "Macha, what is that?" Rinku told, gesturing towards a mountain-like formation. 
 "I'm not sure. We could ask someone around here or look it up online," I suggested. We googled it and found out that it is Uchisar Castle.  The castle is a 60-metre-high 'castle' which is a rock formation visible over a wide distance. It is built on a hilltop overlooking the town and the surrounding desert landscape and is the highest point in the town. It was famous for its panoramic views and sunsets. We decided to catch the sunset from the castle. Our first stop was Pigeon Valley, offering a picturesque view of the castle situated at the far end of the town. We also came across a tree decorated with evil eyes, a local tradition believed to ward off negative energy. While I wasn't particularly fond of such things, Pavithra & Farini tied the evil eye. We later continued on our way to the castle to witness the sunset. The huge castle had steps on its farther side to reach the top to witness the sunset. The massive boulders inside are intricately carved into cave-like structures where one could play hide and seek. We reached to the top reminiscing our childhood days by playing hide and seek. The cool breeze and the contrasting views—on one side, the historical charm of Georme, and on the other, the twinkling city lights of Kapadokya other side added zest to our expectation to catch the amazing sunset.  
 However, luck did not favour us as the blanket of clouds covered the setting sun, plunging the evening into darkness.  We reached back to the city and started hunting for some street food. As we strolled through the streets despite our search, we ended up in an Indian Restaurant.  Having roti and sabjis at India Gate restaurant was not bad after all to end the day. 
 
 15/06/2023 - Kappdokya Sightseeing The previous day when we were discussing where to catch the beautiful sunrise, Farini figured that Love Valley was a perfect place to witness the sunrise and the hot air balloons. Also, read that the valley usually will be crowded with a lot of Instagrammable women waiting to capture the stills amid the scenic beauty. "I found some offbeat location", Farini dinged in. She read out a blog where the author had mentioned another spot in the same valley stating it would be less crowded.  
 We woke up again at 4 a.m. and drove to the location we had to pass the Love Valley viewpoint and it was super crowded. A lot of people with photographers and caravans had tented before even we reached there. We continued to the geo-location which was mentioned in the blog and found a perfect spot. Look at these pictures and probably that would tell you all how the view was. 
 After the scenic shoot, we came back to the hotel and changed into our clothes.  Kaymakli Underground City It was around an hour's drive from our hotel to Kaymakli. Derinkuyu and Kaymakli are the two towns near Cappadocia which have underground cities and it is said that these two cities are connected. According to the reviews, Kaymakli was less crowded and we chose to visit.  We were always concerned about our claustrophobic Rinku 🤣 It is believed that it was used by Christians as a refuge to hide from persecution. It is an 8-storey underground with winding tunnels, storage rooms, ventilation shafts, and underground churches of the city. Out of 8 stories, only 4 were accessible and the path was so narrow that we often felt eerie when we passed through them.  "Would you dare to visit this place during the night times?", My innerme mocked me highlighting my fear for the dark. It was our first time seeing something like this and the whole time we were just analysing how it would have been built in those times. No drilling equipment or excavation tools, yet they had created a perfect place to hide.  Oh by the way, it has separate entrances and exits to each storey and the entrance path is so narrow while the exit is the opposite. We assumed it is because the entry to invaders has to be hard and the path for the refugees to escape should be easier. We spent almost an hour and a half in here and while we were on the way back, we saw two women making something similar to Paratha on the rolling board. We were curious and went to see it. "Gozleme", The lady clarified.  We had seen this word in a lot of menus but we never had an idea it was the Turkish version of Indian Paratha. They had two options, spinach and paneer. We took both and savoured it.  "I want to try that atleast here", Pavithra said pointing to Ayran. Ayran is a Turkish beverage and we had thought that it was buttermilk. But someone in Istanbul had told us that it was yoghurt and we thought might be thick Greek yoghurt. We took one and we tried. Damn, it was a buttermilk.  For a second all our souls got elevated to cloud nine. A proper vegetarian breakfast, Gozleme and Ayran were the perfect duo. Couldn't be more greatful then. We left for Acigol, also called Nar Lake.  
 
 Nar Lake is an offbeat place and it is very less visited. It was just us when we reached.  It is said to have formed from volcanic activity hundreds of years back. A perfect noon to nap on the banks and enjoy the calmness of the water. It was followed by driving through the scenic routes of Naveshir and a cosy rooftop to view the sunset. Did I tell you about Sheesha (hookah) in Turkey? 
It was so damn smooth and one of the best things to do. 
Sheesha is one of the Middle Eastern things that Turkey has. We tried Raki alongside Sheesha. Raki is the national drink of Turkey and is traditionally consumed with chilled water on the side or partly mixed with chilled water. The combined will result in the taste of the milk. 
 What a perfect day to end! 16/06/2023 - Enroute Antalya It was another journey day as we had to travel around 7 hours to reach Antalya. En route, we decided to visit Ilhara Valley. "Are you guys sure you wanna get down to the viewpoint?", I asked everyone before buying the entry tickets. As we went down, there was a small waterfall and a narrow path continued across the stream. We thought we would follow as we might find something more. That mini waterfall did not seem like it was the actual place as we had paid a hefty entry fee.  "Something more would be there", my inner me uttered  As we followed the path, we did not find anything and we had already walked for about 2 km. It was hot and we were already tired, not physically but mentally though as we did not prepare for it. As we decided to hike back we saw a sign board. Kokan Church was still half a mile away and continued walking towards it. It was nothing but ruins with a couple of history boards depicting it. At the stone throw distance, we saw benches to relax and we took a pit stop before returning. While we were taking pictures, I noticed some creepy symbols there.  We went to see what that was and were awestruck. There were more of those creepy figures such as birds, skulls, and weird unrecognisable symbols. There were stairs leading to a room but it was stopped by a small wooden barricade. My wife loves these kinds of weirdly haunting things as much as she weirdly loves haunting me and started climbing those stairs.  
 "Pavithra shut up and come back", Farini shouted  
 "Aye wait, let me see what is in there and come back.", she continued climbing. 
 "What if some ghost enters your body, we have to bear her back home.", she was genuinely scared. 
 I was not bothered greatly as I live with an alternate version of a ghost.   A man fearlessly walked in, asking my wife to excuse him to go up his way; she followed him without thinking twice, and we all ran towards her. Duck, the room that the stairs lead to was his room and he was the night guard of that church. His room was even more scary right from the table to the water pot he had. We ran back from that place as quickly as possible and headed back to Antalya. We passed through the Koprulu Canyon witnessing the white water river rafting. Rafting through the canyons seemed scenic. We instantly booked our rafting tickets for the next day via GetYourGuide and reached Antalya. 17/06/2023 - Koprulu rafting and Antalya 
 I woke up from a sound solid sleep and the Airbnb was way too cozy for that night. After savouring the amazing city view while sipping the Turkish tea, we all got ready for rafting. "Yay, finally my first rafting.", Pavithra started jumping  
 "Me too, me too", Farini hifi-ed It was an hour's ride from Antalya to the pick-up point, Tornado Rafting. As we reached there we had the safety instructions and shoes/sandals were mandatory. We had to buy a new pair of water shoes and follow our guide, Abdul. As we started towards the raft, we had to acclimatize ourselves and had to walk in cold water for 300 mts and then hop onto the raft. We all froze to death for a minute while we were there. It was damn cold and Pavithra & Farini could not even withstand the pain they got from the chillness of the water. As we hopped onto the raft, we got introduced to our fellow mates, a father-son from Niegiera and the other 4 were a group of silly girls from other parts of the world. They were students in France and they all had come for a vacation. God, could not bear their weirdness all the way. It was a 14 km rafting through the great Koprulu Canyons and it was not great for me & Rinku. Of course, it was nice, but it did not meet our expectations of rafting we had in Rishikesh, Uttarakhand & Dandeli, Karnataka. The rapids were not so exciting.  We pulled over for a break and there were a couple of adventure sports like dirt bikes, etc. We just had Gozleme and did our adventure sport, Cliff Jumping. There was a 10ft wooden ramp through which we could jump into the flowing river water and swim back. We all jumped taking turns a few times and that was more amazing than the so-called adventure sport they had there. After an hour, we started rafting towards the destination and reached there around 3 PM. We had a complimentary lunch included, and we headed back to Antalya.  We were completely drained by the time we reached our Airbnb. Slept for an hour and made preps for our outdoor lunch. Tangy veg pulao, Doritos, Beer, and non-stop banter with a city view gave us a perfect climax for the day. 18/06/2023 - Antalya -> Kas "Yahhhh-hhaaaaaa", I stretched my whole body yawning. 
 That satisfaction you get when you have a sound sleep is beyond description. It was a relaxed morning with not many plans apart from the city tour and drive to Kas. We cooked some breakfast and left to explore the city markets. 
 We had heard a lot about Antalya. From the tall scrappers to serene beaches flanked by luxurious hotels, it was beyond our expectations. Unlike Istanbul, Antalya was very much of a European culture. Probably because it is geologically close to Europe.  It has a lot of markets in the main city where they sell all first-copy luxury items such as Prada, Armani, Gucci, etc. Name a brand and they will have it. Despite it being cheap, I felt it was not worth buying a first copy spending thousands of rupees. We took a stroll and headed to Duden Waterfalls. There are two duden, upper and lower. 
 
 The lower Duden directly falls from the cliff joining the Mediterranean Sea whereas the upper Duden flows through Duden Park. 
 There is also a cave where we can witness the falls from behind and the view is just picturesque. It was already noon, we stopped by a street food stall for Gozleme & Ayran. We skipped visiting Antalya beach as we were anyway heading towards Kas.  "Can you please exchange your reservation with our neighbor Airbnb?", Our host at Kas requested us as the previous guest was willing to extend. I was still not sure as the Airbnb we had booked had a beach view and we decided to take a look at the other Airbnb and then give him consent. I would say we hit the jackpot. 
This other Airbnb was way more awesome than the one I had booked. Could not take our eyes off that beach view.  We quickly changed into swimwear and left for the beach. Oh btw, did I tell you that sunsets in Turkey were around 8 PM? It just gave us the privilege to do a lot of activities. Kas has a lot of serene beaches. A lot of them are private beaches attached to the resorts with very few public beaches and one such was Buyuk Beach. As we walked onto the beach, the beach was full of pebbles, unlike sand. The pebbles at the shore were soft and slippery. It was hard for us to even stand there.  Me and Rinku slowly entered the beach and started playing carefully as there were big pebbles inside and holding onto them was quite tough. Farini & Pavithra enjoyed sitting on the shore and took some pictures of us. While we were playing, we saw some local boys, jumping from a cliff at one corner and swimming towards the shore.  
 I was a bit afraid as I did not know the depth of that particular place and also because of the pebbles inside. I was afraid I would get hurt which I do most of the time on the trip.  "Remember the muscle tear in Ziro, Arunachal?", my inner me reminded me of a previous incident. We enjoyed it till the sunset and drove back to our Airbnb. So wondering what's next? 

What would you do if you were in a Turkish-European coastal town with an ideal place for nightlife? We did the same, haha.  The Kas Republic square 
 "What is this place man?", Rinku asked me in awe. The crowds crisscrossed through the open space, roaming around the cobblestone streets with open-air restaurants, pubs and street foods gave us a whole different vibe we never experienced before. The live music from the pubs there was a feast to our ears. It is a joyous spot for everyone to have a good time. We had delicious pizza and a couple of beers there. Of course, it finishes with a famous Turkish dessert, kunafa (Knafeh).  
 Farini would have killed us if we had missed having the dessert there. Out of all the Kunafas we had, Kas was the best. 19/06/2023  Kas -> Fethiye It was a relaxed morning, starting with tea on the sea-view balcony. I guess our stomachs were craving for the sugar rush, so we went to have a kunafa again in the same place. Why am I so obsessed with tea in Turkey?

It is one of the purest tea in the world with no pesticides used in its cultivation. Nevertheless, it tastes so good without much of a sourness highlighting the authentic tea flavour. We started our journey towards Fethiye. Fethiye is known for its turquoise water and also it has some ancient ruins. We checked into our Airbnb hosted by Ozgur. It was an apartment in a small community. "This place has no wifi?", the girls screamed in the unison 
 "Apparently, no", I replied with a blatant face. 
 I was kinda happy to be in a disconnected place. We went to explore the beaches to see how blue it was, and we were amused seriously once we saw Oludeniz Beach. It was a pristine blue beach with pebbles like we saw in Kas.  While we stepped in, the pebbles were not as smooth as we thought. It has big stones, it was very slippery to even stand inside the water. Somehow we ended up playing.  After a while, during sunset, we saw a couple of paragliders swirling in the sky. We had heard that Fethiye has this sport, but were not sure of it. Once we were done with the beach, we took a stroll through the main street enquiring about paragliding and we found the best agency to paraglide with, Big Brothers Travel. We headed back to Airbnb with a couple of beers and Doritos. Had amazing Channa Pulao and slept dreaming about the next day's adventure sport.   20/06/2023 Fethiye -> Lake Salda Can I say it was a tense yet exciting morning for us? It was the first time for us to paraglide except Rinku.  "You fine?", Pavithra checked on me as I tensefully gazed at the people getting lifted by the glider aircraft. 
 I am scared of heights and had zero clue about what I was gonna do standing at the jump-off point. All I was thinking was not to go back as I had already paid for it. Rinku took off, Harini took off and it was my turn next.  I sat on the pod with the captain, Ismail and shut my eyes. I could feel the heaviness and heart skipping its beat. To my fate, the wind speed was so high and it took nearly 20 mins for the pilot to control the direction. At this point all my fear was gone, because we had already taken off to that height and all I could do was, hope and enjoy the beach view. We slowly gained traction and started going towards the beach. By this time, the pilot asked me if I wanted to swirl right and left, and I said yes. He let me handle the harnesses and guided me to change direction. You know what? I did a swirl tooo, haha!!!!!!!!!!!! The pilot eventually directed towards the Butterfly Beach and the bird's eye view was just breathtaking. The pristine blue beach, golden sands, created a captivating contrast. 
 
 I could not take off my eyes it at all. After an hour of flight or so, we slowly descended back safely. After mine, I waited for Pavithra to come.  I do not have any pictures of me taken during the flight as they quoted very high. It was almost to the price of paragliding itself. We thought we better do another round of sport than taking it. Of course, no regrets because Rinku captured a few after he landed. We checked out after the sport and headed towards the Salda. Salda is a very less visited place so we wanted to disconnect from the famous tourist spots. Even Fethiye is one of the less visited places, but Salda is even less visited.  "Rithesh, I guess we could have taken the pictures.", Farini started to regret that we did not buy our paragliding. We were halfway to Salda and we just had to drive ahead without an option. However we ensured, we would buy the next time we do this sport even if it costs a kidney, haha. Salda was a short 3-hour drive and we reached there by late noon. We checked into the only hotel on the lake salda, Lago Di Salda.  The staff were really welcoming and they guided us to take an evening tour to visit the lake through a small Toy Truck Lake Salda gained international attention when NASA scientists visited it to conduct research. Lake Salda was chosen as a test site for instruments and equipment that would be used in the exploration of Mars due to its geological similarities to the red planet. Visitors are not allowed to enter into the waters. We took a couple of pictures from the far sight from the viewpoint and chilled the rest of the evening in the resort. The resort also had access to the lake, but it was mentioned we should not enter into it due to the minerals found and said to be toxic.  Concluding our day with a beer, enjoying the golden hour sunset, and retiring for the night with intimacy. 21/06/2023 Lake Salda -> Pammukkale What a delightful way to start the day! Waking up to the serene beauty of Lake Salda and stretching your arms in the fresh morning air sounds truly rejuvenating.  Hotel Lago di Salda must offer a picturesque view of the lake, providing a perfect setting for relaxation and appreciation of nature's wonders. We had a relaxing breakfast and checked out of the hotel to Pamukkale, known for its Travertine terraces. By the time we arrived in the late afternoon, we realized we wouldn't be able to explore the entire Travertine terraces. Instead, we opted to take a leisurely walk and soak in the atmosphere of the town. "Hey, look at these caves, isn't it something we need to see", Pavithra pointed at a cave picture in one of the ad boards put up in front of some tourist office.  Rinku checked Google images and she showed us how beautiful the Kaklik caves were. We checked the route and distance, it was on the way that could be covered en route to Selcuk.  We picked up a few snacks from the supermarket, along with some beers and vodka, to enjoy and unwind for the rest of our evening. 22/06/2023 - Pammukkale Yet another exciting day for the girls to have some more Instagrammable pictures.  Having a tasty Turkish breakfast, we reached Travertines. As we entered through the travertines, we were supposed to remove our shoes and enter because of the cleanliness.  Can I take the pleasure of spoiling the excitement? Well, let me not do so Pamukkale's travertines are extensive formations composed of calcite, developed over thousands of years. The area features numerous pools containing clear blue water, arranged in terraced patterns similar to rice terraces found in South Asia. These pools are commonly known as thermal pools. The pictures that you look at on the google are very old. Can I say more than a decade old? 
Yes.  The travertine is split into three parts, the first is the white cotton candy structure white thermal pools filled with water from the pipes running at the top. Natural water is hardly found there and it is all filled using pipes and one can observe as you go at the top of the travertine. Running pipes are closed with wooden steps for people not to notice. It was okayish and 5/6 pools had a good amount of water where we could step down and click a few pictures. The second part is where it has more of these thermal pools but does not allow visitors to step in. These pools are relatively good compared to what we saw at first.  Third is where the amphitheatre and Herapolis are there. Romans loved this place and decided to build a city where they could savour the then beauty of Pamukkale. Hierapolis is all ruined now and you need to hike a lot to see the amphi theatre. We just decided to skip that theatre and chill by the Antique pool An expensive place to swim is Cleopatra's antique pool. A pool spread over 150 meters with a hell lot of crowd inside quoted 100 Lira for one hour. Not worth spending that much to bathe there amidst the crowd. Being highly bored, we decided to take a nap in the park next to the pool  
 We could have come back, but we wanted to the sunset from there. As the golden hour started, we went to the second part where there were better thermal pools. The sight was mesmerising and finally, something that was worth witnessing that day. We reached back to the hotel and wrapped our day. 23/06/2023  - Pammukkale -> Selcuk We departed from the hotel and made a stop at Kaklik caves along the way.  The caves at Kaklik had fewer visitors, offering a more secluded experience. 
 Similar to Pamukkale, the caves featured travertine formations, albeit on a smaller scale. The continuous flow of natural water within the caves contributed to the development of these travertines. The water in the area likely has a high calcium content, contributing to the formation of these geological features.  We truly loved and enjoyed this place more than the previous day. We had to stop by for lunch at a roadside small eatery despite we could not find any good restaurants on the way as it was already late. 
 Nevertheless, Farini & Pavithra would have ended up in jail for beheading their husband's head. Afterwards, we arrived in Selcuk and checked into the Rebetika Hotel.  Following our customary routine, we gathered supplies for our evening party and took a stroll, exploring the city's streets and soaking in the local atmosphere. 
 24/06/2023  - Selcuk -> Istanbul It was way too sunny a day with the temperature hitting 35 degrees. While I and Rinku were very excited to see Ephesus, the ancient city,  Farini and Pavithra were taken aback by the day's temperature. We reached Ephesus and before even we headed to the ticket counter, these girls raided the Gelato shops there.  Ephesus, The Ancient City  This is an interesting and beautiful place for someone fond of history and culture. Very similar to our Hampi, Belur and Halebid temples in Karnataka with vast historic significance.  Ephesus has amphitheatres, libraries, stoned pavements, tall pillars decorating the sides of the roads, temples, the Virgin Mary's house and terraced houses showing how wealthy lived their lifestyles back then.  It is very vast and takes a few hours to explore the site.  "It's so hot, we will sit here and you guys go and come", Pavithra said as she could not walk any further after visiting the library. Farini chose to stay as well as she was also tired and probably waiting for Pavithra to say 🤣 I and Rinku explored the whole site and reached back an hour later. We actually enjoyed the site and had our elaborative discussion 
 
 We went inside the ruined library for some pictures and the ladies were again on their feet waiting to rush outside. Probably they wanted to grab another round of Gelatos. We had already packed our bags and we left for Istanbul.  Istanbul was a 6-hour drive from Selcuk, and it was indeed a tiring journey for both of us. Likely, we were physically exhausted. We somehow made it to Istanbul and as said earlier, Istanbul is a place where your money goes down the drain just for parking your cars. We checked into our Airbnb and decided to take a stroll on our favourite Istiklal Street. The Airbnb was good but not the neighbourhood or at least not as great as we had during our first day. That was happening place. Remember that super cute police chick? (Wink Wink) "Let's have one last kunafa here", Farini chimed out of nowhere listening to the plan. She showed one famous restaurant in Istiklal Street costing kidneys just for that dessert. Pun Itended. 
 
 We took a walk as it was quite nearby and headed to Galata Tower. I wanted to see it one last time and to our surprise, the tower had a light show.  
 Ah, one magical evening to cherish our good times in Turkey. It was amazing. We had our last kunafa at the restaurant and walked back to Airbnb, feeling a sense of nostalgia as the trip came to an end. 25/06/2023  - Back to India We had our flight back to Bengaluru at noon.  Checked out our stay had an early breakfast and prepared some food for layovers. Dropped in the car settled the rent and bid adios to Turkey. elveda güle güle (Translated as Adios Amigos) Travellers

Paragliding in Oludeniz is must.

textData.text: Once we had settled on our plans for Iceland and were on the verge of booking our caravan and flights, a moment of hesitation crept in. The allure of Iceland in winter, with its mesmerizing ice caves and breathtaking landscapes, was undeniable.
“What about Turkey and the hot air balloon?”, Rinku proposed.
A brief pause ensued as we exchanged glances, and in that shared moment, our decision was made. We nodded in agreement, swayed by the excitement of a new adventure awaiting us in Turkey.
11/06/2023  - Arrival in Istanbul
The first thing I did was grunt, looking at the long queue for clearing immigration. We already had a long flight and now had to wait an hour again to clear immigration.
Meanwhile, Rinku was in touch with a self-drive rental agency, sorting out the pickup details for our booked car.
Navigating Turkey without Google Translate? Nearly impossible. English speakers are very rare.
As usual, our busy wives started taking their Instagrammable pictures forgetting to do one important thing, to download offline maps to reach our Airbnb.
A tip:
Avoid purchasing sims at the airport due to high prices. Reach Istanbul using offline Google Maps, bargain at some local shops and buy.

Our Fiat Aegea awaited us. Setting off, we were directionless, with neither signboards nor familiarity guiding us. To add to the challenge, the car was left-hand drive. I was at least mentally prepared that my right hand had to hit the gear and not left, etc. But Rinku was clueless. He started driving around the highway and figured it out somehow.
We drove for almost an hour and finally, we were where we started.
"Damn, we are just circuiting the same route.", I sighed.
We were just circuiting around the airport and not going anywhere out.  We stopped our car and decided to ask for help.
A few gentlemen tried to help but couldn’t figure out what they were saying. Turkish words are crazy, it was hard for us to even utter some of them.
Beyoğlu is prononunced as Beeeyoooyulu
Finally, someone was wise enough to share his hotspot and help us in preloading the route.
Istanbul it is

A harmonious blend of European, Turkish, and Arabic influences, it felt like the my home town Bengaluru of Turkey. Remarkably, despite its heavy reliance on tourism and limited exports, the city offered top-notch infrastructure.

As we drove through the streets of Istanbul we entered Taksim Square and at one road junction, we were kind of confused about how to navigate straight as it seemed like a very narrow road. While we just thought it could be the wrong route as Google Maps never leads us to the right route most of the time, A super cute lady came and signalled us to go the same way. Damn, she was a cop.
While I was still awestruck by her cuteness, the jealous Rinku drove off.
After a few more turns, we reached our Airbnb at Yani Carsi Caddesi  ('Caddesi' translates to 'Street' in Turkish).
Despite the exterior looking very old, the interior of the Airbnb was way too nice. A typical Turkish house with artistic wooden cladding and high ceilings.
We got some time to chill and were super hungry. We had taken some ready-made food as we had core vegetarians in our group.
"I want peas pulao", I chimed in when Farini & Pavithra were about to open those food packets.
It was already evening by then with very little energy. We did not want to take our car out for a spin again and searched for a nearby place.
Galata Bridge was within walking distance (that's what we thought).

We walked through the narrow streets of Beyoglu and reached there.  The Galata Bridge is very famous and also overrated as there is nothing much to do, except if you want to take a Bosphorus cruise ride. It has a few fancy restaurants facing toward the waterfront where you can savour some good seafood.
It was quite popular as it connects the two parts of Istanbul. Also said that it just did not connect places, but also culture and people.
We indeed struggled to walk back as I said, it was not really at a walkable distance.
12/06/2023 - Istanbul Sightseeing
We were super excited to see the places in Istanbul. I honestly don't know what made us so touristy this time, Haha!!!!

We first drove to Topkapi Palace. But, it was closed due to weekly cleaning. Unfortunate? No, It was fortunate that I got to skip one crowded place. The next place was the Blue Mosque. We had heard a lot about its beauty thought.
I lost all the excitement while figuring out where to park our car.
Sighed in relief when I finally found one.
"These paid parking places cost a kidney", I said looking at the hourly price.
"Your kidney is useless anyway, chill.", Pavithra mocked and dragged me as we were already running late.

The Blue Mosque is renowned for its stunning architecture, which indeed offers a picturesque sight to behold. The mosque derives its name from the magnificent blue tiles adorning its interior walls, creating a mesmerizing visual effect. As we took a moment to soak in the ambience, our wives, ever eager to capture the beauty, walked out.

Just opposite the mosque stood the Hagia Sophia Church, another architectural marvel of Istanbul. As we walked through the corridor, we found some street food options. Nutella bun and fried water chestnuts were delightful treats. Pavithra loved chestnuts more than she loved me.
As we approached the Hagia Sophia, we all turned unanimously and started walking back, LOL.
It was so crowded that the line stretched over a kilometre, signalling an overcrowded interior. It was not our cup of tea.

As we made our way back to the car, our wives' eyes spotted the renowned Turkish ice cream stand. You've likely come across those playful Instagram videos where vendors engage in amusing stunts before handing over the cone. Indeed, that's the famous Turkish gelato for you, as delightful in taste as it is in its playful presentation.

We got fooled there without asking for the price first and ended up paying around 180 TL (approx 700 INR). They will first start playing and keep adding more scoops to charge extra. It does not happen everywhere, but it did occur in the central city of Istanbul.
(Always ask the price and take one scoop. Do not let him put 3/4 scoops and charge you heavy for the fun he has.)
We took our car and left for Balat Street. It is probably a less explored place I felt.
Every street in there was unique. One lane had colourful houses of Balat, while the other was full of graffiti-walled buildings. Nevertheless, the street with full of cafes and gelato ice creams.
We had a good lunch there and left for Galata Tower. It was very close by so we decided to park our car and explore the streets of Taksim Square.

The street adjacent to our accommodation was none other than Istiklal Caddesi, the liveliest street in Istanbul. This bustling avenue offers a diverse shopping experience, featuring everything from luxury brands to local shops, ensuring a plethora of choices for every shopper.  Adding to its charm, the street has a super cute tram that shuttles passengers along its length, adding a touch of nostalgia to the vibrant atmosphere.
The end of this street is where Galata Tower is. Qutub Minar version of Istanbul, I felt.

textData.text: The view of the tower was amazing, but we felt disappointed with the price we had to pay to ascend to the top of the tower to witness the city's panoramic view. Some said, overrated while some said it was a must-do. Battling that confusion, we decided not to go.
We reached back to our Airbnb cooked some food and wrapped up our busy day.
Cappadocia

We began our journey early, expecting a drive of around 800 km and possibly spanning 10-12 hours. However, the actual travel time turned out to be considerably less. The road conditions were notably good, with a single highway linking Cappadocia to Istanbul, covering a distance of approximately 7330 km.

textData.text: Around 1 AM, we decided to make a pit stop at a restaurant that offered outdoor seating. The ambience was pleasant and spacious, but no printed menu. The staff used to blurt it out and deciphering was harder than my post-graduate exam.
"Mattu, mulberries", exclaimed my kid (wife) and ran towards the mulberry trees over there.

There were two simultaneous plays. 

Firstly, the challenge in communicating with staff to order something to eat. Secondly, my wife's pursuit of mulberries. 

She was least bothered about the food.
Gasping the beauty of the sun going down the horizon, we finally reached Cappadocia and settled into our cave hotel.
Kapadokya is a Turkish name for Cappadocia (Derived from persian language)
Cappadocia is beyond description.
The whole vibe was different. Istanbul was more of a party and happening place, whereas this had an authentic Turkish experience, offering stunning valleys and unique cave formations.

Staying in an authentic cave hotel is an experience not to be missed. We were fortunate to stay right in the city centre, allowing us the convenience of a stroll to discover nearby eateries and gelato shops in anticipation of the following day's adventures.
14/06/2023 - Hot Air Balloon ride
"Yaaaaaay, the hot air balloon adventure is finally here!" my inner voice cheered with excitement.
Today marked the highly anticipated day of our Turkey trip.
Promptly at 4 AM, a Mercedes van arrived at our hotel to transport us to the hot air balloon launch site.
Damn, people in Turkey are crazy enough to keep Mercedes for pickup vehicles.

Having pre-booked our hot air balloon adventure through GetYourGuide, we had selected the option for pick-up and drop-off services. The sites chosen for take-off and landing can vary depending on the prevailing wind conditions.
We were amazed to see the balloons getting inflated at the campsite. We soon jumped out of the vehicle and approached the majestic balloons.
Take-off Phase

The initial phase involved fixing the parachute to the top of the balloon, followed by inflating it with air. Subsequently, the crew loaded the gas cylinders and connected them to the burners within the balloon's interior. Once preparations were complete, they elevated the balloon, allowing us to board the designated compartments within the Gondola box or wicker basket. This rectangular basket is divided into eight sections, typically accommodating 3 or 4 passengers per section, depending on the group
size.
As the crew released the tethering ropes, the balloon began its ascent.
My inner me started scaring the shit out of me.
"What if the gondola box cuts off the thread?",
"What if the balloon ruptures mid-air?
Taking a deep breath, I reassured myself, "Relax, I've got travel insurance,".
Flying the Ballon
The captain skillfully handled the balloon using the four burners, each one determining the balloon's direction and regulating its altitude.

textData.text: As it took off to a certain height, the excitement increased every second to witness how magical it would be.
As the first rays of sunlight painted the sky with hues of pink and gold, setting against the backdrop of a hundred balloons dotting the sky.
We were left in sheer wonder. It was a moment that seemed to suspend time itself.
Landing Phase
After zooming through the skies for an hour, the captains began preparations for the descent. Taking into account the current wind patterns, they select the landing site.

Signalling to the ground crew, the captains steered the balloon towards the designated landing area. While the flight itself was a thrilling experience, the landing process demanded attention and skill.
As the balloon neared the ground, a rope was tossed overboard, enabling the ground crew to gradually pull and control the balloon for a smooth landing.
After landing - Party scenes
Every flight of the balloon is celebrated with the champagnes as it was how the inventors Joseph-Michel and Jacques-Étienne Montgolfier celebrated
Upon returning to our hotel, we quickly changed into more relaxed attire. Eager to continue our exploration, we set out to discover Kapadokya.

Navigating with our maps, we started towards the Red Valley, which had mesmerized us during our hot air balloon ride. However, we were not at all surprised when we ended up in the untouched grasslands— of course, it was Google Maps after all.
Started to drive back towards the city and stumbled upon a path leading to Love Valley.

Wondering what's with these valleys in Kapadokya?
Kapadokya is renowned for its diverse array of valleys, each characterized by its unique terrain and allure.
The route we just found to the love valley, was the hiking route. We parked our car and followed the path. As we went further ahead, the girls were tired.

It wasn't long before we encountered the distinctive rock formations that the valley is renowned for—tall towery structures bearing a resemblance to Penis. Indeed, the entire landscape was dominated by these unique formations, which probably indicates why it's called Love Valley.

textData.text: As lunchtime approached, we decided to explore Diverent Valley and Pasabga Valley. While Diverent Valley was okayish, Pasabga Valley was unique with its rock formations.
Both valleys also had a few souvenir shops, offering a range of souvenirs at relatively affordable prices compared to other tourist spots we had visited.
"Macha, what is that?" Rinku told, gesturing towards a mountain-like formation.
"I'm not sure. We could ask someone around here or look it up online," I suggested.
We googled it and found out that it is Uchisar Castle.

The castle is a 60-metre-high 'castle' which is a rock formation visible over a wide distance. It is built on a hilltop overlooking the town and the surrounding desert landscape and is the highest point in the town. It was famous for its panoramic views and sunsets. We decided to catch the sunset from the castle.

Our first stop was Pigeon Valley, offering a picturesque view of the castle situated at the far end of the town. We also came across a tree decorated with evil eyes, a local tradition believed to ward off negative energy. While I wasn't particularly fond of such things, Pavithra & Farini tied the evil eye. We later continued on our way to the castle to witness the sunset.

imageData.caption: The evil's eye staring at the evil eye tree, haha!!

textData.text: The huge castle had steps on its farther side to reach the top to witness the sunset. The massive boulders inside are intricately carved into cave-like structures where one could play hide and seek. We reached to the top reminiscing our childhood days by playing hide and seek.

textData.text: The cool breeze and the contrasting views—on one side, the historical charm of Georme, and on the other, the twinkling city lights of Kapadokya other side added zest to our expectation to catch the amazing sunset.
However, luck did not favour us as the blanket of clouds covered the setting sun, plunging the evening into darkness.
We reached back to the city and started hunting for some street food. As we strolled through the streets despite our search, we ended up in an Indian Restaurant.
Having roti and sabjis at India Gate restaurant was not bad after all to end the day.
15/06/2023 - Kappdokya Sightseeing

The previous day when we were discussing where to catch the beautiful sunrise, Farini figured that Love Valley was a perfect place to witness the sunrise and the hot air balloons. Also, read that the valley usually will be crowded with a lot of Instagrammable women waiting to capture the stills amid the scenic beauty.
"I found some offbeat location", Farini dinged in.
She read out a blog where the author had mentioned another spot in the same valley stating it would be less crowded.

We woke up again at 4 a.m. and drove to the location we had to pass the Love Valley viewpoint and it was super crowded. A lot of people with photographers and caravans had tented before even we reached there. We continued to the geo-location which was mentioned in the blog and found a perfect spot.
Look at these pictures and probably that would tell you all how the view was.

textData.text: After the scenic shoot, we came back to the hotel and changed into our clothes.
Kaymakli Underground City

It was around an hour's drive from our hotel to Kaymakli. Derinkuyu and Kaymakli are the two towns near Cappadocia which have underground cities and it is said that these two cities are connected. According to the reviews, Kaymakli was less crowded and we chose to visit.
We were always concerned about our claustrophobic Rinku 🤣

It is believed that it was used by Christians as a refuge to hide from persecution. It is an 8-storey underground with winding tunnels, storage rooms, ventilation shafts, and underground churches of the city. Out of 8 stories, only 4 were accessible and the path was so narrow that we often felt eerie when we passed through them.

textData.text: "Would you dare to visit this place during the night times?", My innerme mocked me highlighting my fear for the dark.

It was our first time seeing something like this and the whole time we were just analysing how it would have been built in those times. No drilling equipment or excavation tools, yet they had created a perfect place to hide.

Oh by the way, it has separate entrances and exits to each storey and the entrance path is so narrow while the exit is the opposite. We assumed it is because the entry to invaders has to be hard and the path for the refugees to escape should be easier.
We spent almost an hour and a half in here and while we were on the way back, we saw two women making something similar to Paratha on the rolling board. We were curious and went to see it.
"Gozleme", The lady clarified.
We had seen this word in a lot of menus but we never had an idea it was the Turkish version of Indian Paratha. They had two options, spinach and paneer. We took both and savoured it.
"I want to try that atleast here", Pavithra said pointing to Ayran.
Ayran is a Turkish beverage and we had thought that it was buttermilk. But someone in Istanbul had told us that it was yoghurt and we thought might be thick Greek yoghurt.
We took one and we tried. Damn, it was a buttermilk.
For a second all our souls got elevated to cloud nine. A proper vegetarian breakfast, Gozleme and Ayran were the perfect duo. Couldn't be more greatful then.
We left for Acigol, also called Nar Lake.
Nar Lake is an offbeat place and it is very less visited. It was just us when we reached.
It is said to have formed from volcanic activity hundreds of years back.
A perfect noon to nap on the banks and enjoy the calmness of the water.

textData.text: It was followed by driving through the scenic routes of Naveshir and a cosy rooftop to view the sunset.

Did I tell you about Sheesha (hookah) in Turkey? 
It was so damn smooth and one of the best things to do. 
Sheesha is one of the Middle Eastern things that Turkey has.
We tried Raki alongside Sheesha.
Raki is the national drink of Turkey and is traditionally consumed with chilled water on the side or partly mixed with chilled water. The combined will result in the taste of the milk.
What a perfect day to end!
16/06/2023 - Enroute Antalya
It was another journey day as we had to travel around 7 hours to reach Antalya. En route, we decided to visit Ilhara Valley.
"Are you guys sure you wanna get down to the viewpoint?", I asked everyone before buying the entry tickets.

As we went down, there was a small waterfall and a narrow path continued across the stream. We thought we would follow as we might find something more. That mini waterfall did not seem like it was the actual place as we had paid a hefty entry fee.
"Something more would be there", my inner me uttered
As we followed the path, we did not find anything and we had already walked for about 2 km. It was hot and we were already tired, not physically but mentally though as we did not prepare for it.
As we decided to hike back we saw a sign board.

Kokan Church was still half a mile away and continued walking towards it. It was nothing but ruins with a couple of history boards depicting it. At the stone throw distance, we saw benches to relax and we took a pit stop before returning.
While we were taking pictures, I noticed some creepy symbols there.

We went to see what that was and were awestruck. There were more of those creepy figures such as birds, skulls, and weird unrecognisable symbols. There were stairs leading to a room but it was stopped by a small wooden barricade.
My wife loves these kinds of weirdly haunting things as much as she weirdly loves haunting me and started climbing those stairs.
"Pavithra shut up and come back", Farini shouted
"Aye wait, let me see what is in there and come back.", she continued climbing.
"What if some ghost enters your body, we have to bear her back home.", she was genuinely scared.
I was not bothered greatly as I live with an alternate version of a ghost.
A man fearlessly walked in, asking my wife to excuse him to go up his way; she followed him without thinking twice, and we all ran towards her.

Duck, the room that the stairs lead to was his room and he was the night guard of that church. His room was even more scary right from the table to the water pot he had. We ran back from that place as quickly as possible and headed back to Antalya.

We passed through the Koprulu Canyon witnessing the white water river rafting. Rafting through the canyons seemed scenic. We instantly booked our rafting tickets for the next day via GetYourGuide and reached Antalya.
17/06/2023 - Koprulu rafting and Antalya
I woke up from a sound solid sleep and the Airbnb was way too cozy for that night. After savouring the amazing city view while sipping the Turkish tea, we all got ready for rafting.
"Yay, finally my first rafting.", Pavithra started jumping
"Me too, me too", Farini hifi-ed

It was an hour's ride from Antalya to the pick-up point, Tornado Rafting. As we reached there we had the safety instructions and shoes/sandals were mandatory. We had to buy a new pair of water shoes and follow our guide, Abdul.

As we started towards the raft, we had to acclimatize ourselves and had to walk in cold water for 300 mts and then hop onto the raft. We all froze to death for a minute while we were there. It was damn cold and Pavithra & Farini could not even withstand the pain they got from the chillness of the water. As we hopped onto the raft, we got introduced to our fellow mates, a father-son from Niegiera and the other 4 were a group of silly girls from other parts of the world. They were students in France and they all had come for a vacation. God, could not bear their weirdness all the way.

It was a 14 km rafting through the great Koprulu Canyons and it was not great for me & Rinku. Of course, it was nice, but it did not meet our expectations of rafting we had in Rishikesh, Uttarakhand & Dandeli, Karnataka. The rapids were not so exciting.
We pulled over for a break and there were a couple of adventure sports like dirt bikes, etc. We just had Gozleme and did our adventure sport, Cliff Jumping.

There was a 10ft wooden ramp through which we could jump into the flowing river water and swim back. We all jumped taking turns a few times and that was more amazing than the so-called adventure sport they had there.
After an hour, we started rafting towards the destination and reached there around 3 PM. We had a complimentary lunch included, and we headed back to Antalya.
We were completely drained by the time we reached our Airbnb. Slept for an hour and made preps for our outdoor lunch.
Tangy veg pulao, Doritos, Beer, and non-stop banter with a city view gave us a perfect climax for the day.
18/06/2023 - Antalya -> Kas
"Yahhhh-hhaaaaaa", I stretched my whole body yawning.
That satisfaction you get when you have a sound sleep is beyond description.
It was a relaxed morning with not many plans apart from the city tour and drive to Kas. We cooked some breakfast and left to explore the city markets.
We had heard a lot about Antalya.

From the tall scrappers to serene beaches flanked by luxurious hotels, it was beyond our expectations. Unlike Istanbul, Antalya was very much of a European culture. Probably because it is geologically close to Europe.
It has a lot of markets in the main city where they sell all first-copy luxury items such as Prada, Armani, Gucci, etc.
Name a brand and they will have it. Despite it being cheap, I felt it was not worth buying a first copy spending thousands of rupees. We took a stroll and headed to Duden Waterfalls.

textData.text: There are two duden, upper and lower.
The lower Duden directly falls from the cliff joining the Mediterranean Sea whereas the upper Duden flows through Duden Park.
There is also a cave where we can witness the falls from behind and the view is just picturesque.
It was already noon, we stopped by a street food stall for Gozleme & Ayran. We skipped visiting Antalya beach as we were anyway heading towards Kas.
"Can you please exchange your reservation with our neighbor Airbnb?", Our host at Kas requested us as the previous guest was willing to extend.
I was still not sure as the Airbnb we had booked had a beach view and we decided to take a look at the other Airbnb and then give him consent.

I would say we hit the jackpot. 
This other Airbnb was way more awesome than the one I had booked. Could not take our eyes off that beach view.
We quickly changed into swimwear and left for the beach.
Oh btw, did I tell you that sunsets in Turkey were around 8 PM? It just gave us the privilege to do a lot of activities.
Kas has a lot of serene beaches. A lot of them are private beaches attached to the resorts with very few public beaches and one such was Buyuk Beach.
As we walked onto the beach, the beach was full of pebbles, unlike sand. The pebbles at the shore were soft and slippery. It was hard for us to even stand there.
Me and Rinku slowly entered the beach and started playing carefully as there were big pebbles inside and holding onto them was quite tough.
Farini & Pavithra enjoyed sitting on the shore and took some pictures of us. While we were playing, we saw some local boys, jumping from a cliff at one corner and swimming towards the shore.

textData.text: I was a bit afraid as I did not know the depth of that particular place and also because of the pebbles inside. I was afraid I would get hurt which I do most of the time on the trip.
"Remember the muscle tear in Ziro, Arunachal?", my inner me reminded me of a previous incident.
We enjoyed it till the sunset and drove back to our Airbnb.

So wondering what's next? 

What would you do if you were in a Turkish-European coastal town with an ideal place for nightlife? We did the same, haha.
The Kas Republic square

textData.text: "What is this place man?", Rinku asked me in awe.

The crowds crisscrossed through the open space, roaming around the cobblestone streets with open-air restaurants, pubs and street foods gave us a whole different vibe we never experienced before. The live music from the pubs there was a feast to our ears. It is a joyous spot for everyone to have a good time.
We had delicious pizza and a couple of beers there. Of course, it finishes with a famous Turkish dessert, kunafa (Knafeh).
Farini would have killed us if we had missed having the dessert there.
Out of all the Kunafas we had, Kas was the best.
19/06/2023  Kas -> Fethiye

imageData.caption: The turkish tea with a European view

textData.text: It was a relaxed morning, starting with tea on the sea-view balcony. I guess our stomachs were craving for the sugar rush, so we went to have a kunafa again in the same place.

Why am I so obsessed with tea in Turkey?

It is one of the purest tea in the world with no pesticides used in its cultivation. Nevertheless, it tastes so good without much of a sourness highlighting the authentic tea flavour.

We started our journey towards Fethiye. Fethiye is known for its turquoise water and also it has some ancient ruins. We checked into our Airbnb hosted by Ozgur. It was an apartment in a small community.
"This place has no wifi?", the girls screamed in the unison
"Apparently, no", I replied with a blatant face.
I was kinda happy to be in a disconnected place.
We went to explore the beaches to see how blue it was, and we were amused seriously once we saw Oludeniz Beach. It was a pristine blue beach with pebbles like we saw in Kas.
While we stepped in, the pebbles were not as smooth as we thought. It has big stones, it was very slippery to even stand inside the water. Somehow we ended up playing.
After a while, during sunset, we saw a couple of paragliders swirling in the sky. We had heard that Fethiye has this sport, but were not sure of it.
Once we were done with the beach, we took a stroll through the main street enquiring about paragliding and we found the best agency to paraglide with, Big Brothers Travel.
We headed back to Airbnb with a couple of beers and Doritos. Had amazing Channa Pulao and slept dreaming about the next day's adventure sport.
20/06/2023 Fethiye -> Lake Salda
Can I say it was a tense yet exciting morning for us? It was the first time for us to paraglide except Rinku.
"You fine?", Pavithra checked on me as I tensefully gazed at the people getting lifted by the glider aircraft.
I am scared of heights and had zero clue about what I was gonna do standing at the jump-off point. All I was thinking was not to go back as I had already paid for it.
Rinku took off, Harini took off and it was my turn next.

I sat on the pod with the captain, Ismail and shut my eyes. I could feel the heaviness and heart skipping its beat. To my fate, the wind speed was so high and it took nearly 20 mins for the pilot to control the direction. At this point all my fear was gone, because we had already taken off to that height and all I could do was, hope and enjoy the beach view.
We slowly gained traction and started going towards the beach. By this time, the pilot asked me if I wanted to swirl right and left, and I said yes.
He let me handle the harnesses and guided me to change direction.
You know what? I did a swirl tooo, haha!!!!!!!!!!!!
The pilot eventually directed towards the Butterfly Beach and the bird's eye view was just breathtaking. The pristine blue beach,
golden sands, created a captivating contrast.

imageData.caption: The picture is taken from the google which seemed exactly like it.

textData.text: I could not take off my eyes it at all. After an hour of flight or so, we slowly descended back safely. After mine, I waited for Pavithra to come.

I do not have any pictures of me taken during the flight as they quoted very high. It was almost to the price of paragliding itself. We thought we better do another round of sport than taking it. Of course, no regrets because Rinku captured a few after he landed.

We checked out after the sport and headed towards the Salda. Salda is a very less visited place so we wanted to disconnect from the famous tourist spots. Even Fethiye is one of the less visited places, but Salda is even less visited.
"Rithesh, I guess we could have taken the pictures.", Farini started to regret that we did not buy our paragliding.
We were halfway to Salda and we just had to drive ahead without an option. However we ensured, we would buy the next time we do this sport even if it costs a kidney, haha.
Salda was a short 3-hour drive and we reached there by late noon. We checked into the only hotel on the lake salda, Lago Di Salda.
The staff were really welcoming and they guided us to take an evening tour to visit the lake through a small Toy Truck

imageData.caption: The toy truck suttling passengers from parking to Lake salda view point

textData.text: Lake Salda gained international attention when NASA scientists visited it to conduct research. Lake Salda was chosen as a test site for instruments and equipment that would be used in the exploration of Mars due to its geological similarities to the red planet.

Visitors are not allowed to enter into the waters. We took a couple of pictures from the far sight from the viewpoint and chilled the rest of the evening in the resort. The resort also had access to the lake, but it was mentioned we should not enter into it due to the minerals found and said to be toxic.
Concluding our day with a beer, enjoying the golden hour sunset, and retiring for the night with intimacy.
21/06/2023 Lake Salda -> Pammukkale
What a delightful way to start the day! Waking up to the serene beauty of Lake Salda and stretching your arms in the fresh morning air sounds truly rejuvenating.
Hotel Lago di Salda must offer a picturesque view of the lake, providing a perfect setting for relaxation and appreciation of nature's wonders.
We had a relaxing breakfast and checked out of the hotel to Pamukkale, known for its Travertine terraces.

By the time we arrived in the late afternoon, we realized we wouldn't be able to explore the entire Travertine terraces. Instead, we opted to take a leisurely walk and soak in the atmosphere of the town.
"Hey, look at these caves, isn't it something we need to see", Pavithra pointed at a cave picture in one of the ad boards put up in front of some tourist office.
Rinku checked Google images and she showed us how beautiful the Kaklik caves were. We checked the route and distance, it was on the way that could be covered en route to Selcuk.
We picked up a few snacks from the supermarket, along with some beers and vodka, to enjoy and unwind for the rest of our evening.
22/06/2023 - Pammukkale
Yet another exciting day for the girls to have some more Instagrammable pictures.
Having a tasty Turkish breakfast, we reached Travertines. As we entered through the travertines, we were supposed to remove our shoes and enter because of the cleanliness.
Can I take the pleasure of spoiling the excitement? Well, let me not do so

Pamukkale's travertines are extensive formations composed of calcite, developed over thousands of years. The area features numerous pools containing clear blue water, arranged in terraced patterns similar to rice terraces found in South Asia. These pools are commonly known as thermal pools.

The pictures that you look at on the google are very old. Can I say more than a decade old? 
Yes.

The travertine is split into three parts, the first is the white cotton candy structure white thermal pools filled with water from the pipes running at the top. Natural water is hardly found there and it is all filled using pipes and one can observe as you go at the top of the travertine. Running pipes are closed with wooden steps for people not to notice.
It was okayish and 5/6 pools had a good amount of water where we could step down and click a few pictures.

textData.text: The second part is where it has more of these thermal pools but does not allow visitors to step in. These pools are relatively good compared to what we saw at first.

Third is where the amphitheatre and Herapolis are there. Romans loved this place and decided to build a city where they could savour the then beauty of Pamukkale. Hierapolis is all ruined now and you need to hike a lot to see the amphi theatre. We just decided to skip that theatre and chill by the Antique pool
An expensive place to swim is Cleopatra's antique pool.
A pool spread over 150 meters with a hell lot of crowd inside quoted 100 Lira for one hour.
Not worth spending that much to bathe there amidst the crowd.
Being highly bored, we decided to take a nap in the park next to the pool

We reached back to the hotel and wrapped our day.
23/06/2023  - Pammukkale -> Selcuk
We departed from the hotel and made a stop at Kaklik caves along the way.
The caves at Kaklik had fewer visitors, offering a more secluded experience.

textData.text: Similar to Pamukkale, the caves featured travertine formations, albeit on a smaller scale. The continuous flow of natural water within the caves contributed to the development of these travertines. The water in the area likely has a high calcium content, contributing to the formation of these geological features.
We truly loved and enjoyed this place more than the previous day.
We had to stop by for lunch at a roadside small eatery despite we could not find any good restaurants on the way as it was already late.
Nevertheless, Farini & Pavithra would have ended up in jail for beheading their husband's head.
Afterwards, we arrived in Selcuk and checked into the Rebetika Hotel.
Following our customary routine, we gathered supplies for our evening party and took a stroll, exploring the city's streets and soaking in the local atmosphere.
24/06/2023  - Selcuk -> Istanbul
It was way too sunny a day with the temperature hitting 35 degrees.
While I and Rinku were very excited to see Ephesus, the ancient city,
Farini and Pavithra were taken aback by the day's temperature.
We reached Ephesus and before even we headed to the ticket counter, these girls raided the Gelato shops there.
Ephesus, The Ancient City
This is an interesting and beautiful place for someone fond of history and culture. Very similar to our Hampi, Belur and Halebid temples in Karnataka with vast historic significance.

Ephesus has amphitheatres, libraries, stoned pavements, tall pillars decorating the sides of the roads, temples, the Virgin Mary's house and terraced houses showing how wealthy lived their lifestyles back then.
It is very vast and takes a few hours to explore the site.
"It's so hot, we will sit here and you guys go and come", Pavithra said as she could not walk any further after visiting the library.
Farini chose to stay as well as she was also tired and probably waiting for Pavithra to say 🤣

textData.text: I and Rinku explored the whole site and reached back an hour later. We actually enjoyed the site and had our elaborative discussion
We went inside the ruined library for some pictures and the ladies were again on their feet waiting to rush outside. Probably they wanted to grab another round of Gelatos.
We had already packed our bags and we left for Istanbul.
Istanbul was a 6-hour drive from Selcuk, and it was indeed a tiring journey for both of us. Likely, we were physically exhausted.
We somehow made it to Istanbul and as said earlier, Istanbul is a place where your money goes down the drain just for parking your cars.

We checked into our Airbnb and decided to take a stroll on our favourite Istiklal Street. The Airbnb was good but not the neighbourhood or at least not as great as we had during our first day. That was happening place. Remember that super cute police chick? (Wink Wink)
"Let's have one last kunafa here", Farini chimed out of nowhere listening to the plan. She showed one famous restaurant in Istiklal Street costing kidneys just for that dessert. Pun Itended.
We took a walk as it was quite nearby and headed to Galata Tower. I wanted to see it one last time and to our surprise, the tower had a light show.
Ah, one magical evening to cherish our good times in Turkey. It was amazing.
We had our last kunafa at the restaurant and walked back to Airbnb, feeling a sense of nostalgia as the trip came to an end.
25/06/2023  - Back to India
We had our flight back to Bengaluru at noon.
Checked out our stay had an early breakfast and prepared some food for layovers. Dropped in the car settled the rent and bid adios to Turkey.
